chemistry.crude-extended-items.0012.all: Plan: burning fossil fuels releases CO2 (and CH4 from extraction); greenhouse gases absorb IR re-emitted from Earth, enhanced greenhouse effect, global warming -> climate change. Reduce: renewables/nuclear, efficiency, carbon capture, biofuels/hydrogen, less travel.

chemistry.electrolysis-explain-items.000.all: Cu2+ ions (cause blue colour) are discharged at cathode as copper (Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu); concentration of Cu2+ falls and they are not replaced (inert anode).

chemistry.electrolysis-extended-items.00.all: Plan: ions free to move when molten; Na+ to cathode, Na+ + e- -> Na, sodium metal (silvery liquid); Cl- to anode, 2Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e-, chlorine gas, green, bleaches damp blue litmus. Cathode reduction, anode oxidation.

chemistry.electrolysis-practical-items.0.all: Collect gas in a test tube over cathode; hold lit splint at mouth - squeaky pop.

chemistry.energetics-explain-items.0003.all: Dissolving is exothermic; energy released (more energy released forming bonds/ion-water attraction than taken in) transfers heat to surroundings/water.

chemistry.energetics-practical-items.000.all: Measure fixed volume (e.g. 25 cm3) CuSO4 into polystyrene cup (with lid, in beaker); record initial temperature; add excess zinc powder (weighed), stir; record highest temperature; change = max - initial.

chemistry.energetics-temp-graph.0016.a: Plot points; rising line through 0-15 cm3, falling line through 20-50 cm3
chemistry.energetics-temp-graph.0016.c: Reaction complete/all alkali neutralised so no more heat released; excess cold acid added absorbs heat and cools the mixture, plus heat lost to surroundings.

chemistry.equilibria-explain-items.0003.all: Yield decreases; forward reaction exothermic so equilibrium shifts left (endothermic direction) to oppose the rise in temperature.

chemistry.equilibria-recall-facts.0004.all: Rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal; concentrations of reactants and products stay constant (closed system).

chemistry.equilibria-yield-data.0002.b: Yield decreases as temperature increases; yield increases as pressure increases
chemistry.equilibria-yield-data.0002.c: Exothermic; yield falls when temperature rises so equilibrium shifts in endothermic (backward) direction at higher T
chemistry.equilibria-yield-data.0002.d: Low temperature gives a slow rate; moderate temperature is a compromise giving acceptable yield at faster rate (and catalyst works)

chemistry.extraction-data.0003.b: aluminium; very good resistance to corrosion (also low density)
chemistry.extraction-data.0003.c: Steel (iron) corrodes/rusts in air and water, paint is a barrier; gold is very unreactive so does not corrode

chemistry.extraction-explain-items.0008.all: Aluminium has a much lower density so cables are lighter (fewer pylons) and it is cheaper; also resists corrosion; still a good conductor.

chemistry.extraction-mcq-facts.0008.all: it does not react with water

chemistry.extraction-recall-facts.0004.all: Aircraft bodies - low density and strong (or saucepans - good conductor of heat, resists corrosion)

chemistry.formulae-mgo-data.0004.a: Plot points; straight line through origin with gradient ~0.25
chemistry.formulae-mgo-data.0004.b: 0.25 g, 0.047 g; not heated long enough so not all copper reacted (or lid not lifted)
